subtitle: Two towns share a supernatural problem

body: Yo-kai Watch 3 is Level-5's Nintendo 3DS role-playing adventure following two protagonists in connected settings. Nate moves to the American-inspired town of BBQ, while Hailey Anne Thomas becomes involved with a detective agency in Springdale. Their separate journeys introduce another population of Yo-kai and gradually connect their discoveries. Japan first received Sushi and Tempura versions, followed by the expanded Sukiyaki edition on which the later international release was based. The change of place gives the series' everyday supernatural comedy another community and another young investigator to follow.

Combat replaces the earlier rotating medal arrangement with the Tactics Board, allowing active Yo-kai to be moved around a grid. Their position becomes a practical concern during the fight, changing how the team responds to incoming attacks and makes use of the available space. The player continues to intervene while companions perform their ordinary actions automatically. This reworking gives the sequel a different physical rhythm on the touchscreen. Preparing a capable collection remains important, but positioning the current group adds another immediate decision within an encounter.

Moving between Nate's life in BBQ and Hailey Anne's investigations gives the adventure two different routes into its mysteries. A new town supplies unfamiliar places and creatures, while returning to Springdale allows a different protagonist to encounter the established setting. The expanded international version gathers material from the Japanese releases into one journey. Its larger structure makes collecting and meeting Yo-kai part of two stories at once, using the contrast between familiar surroundings and a new home to keep the hidden world open to discovery.
